lessons.title: Task and audience
lessons.subtitle: Week 6: Prompting with purpose
lessons.body:
A useful prompt specifies the task and intended audience. A request to explain a topic to a beginner is more directed than a request to explain everything.

Offline practice: Write a prompt explaining fractions to a beginner using two examples. Write your reasoning before looking at the quiz answers. Record one limitation or uncertainty. You can use paper or local notes; an online AI tool is optional.

Recap: explain yesterday’s key idea from memory, then check your notes. After a break, start with this recap and the first small step of today’s activity.

Complete all three quiz questions before moving on.
takeaways: A useful prompt specifies the task and intended audience. A request to explain a topic to a beginner is more directed than a request to explain everything.
Apply the idea through the offline activity.
Keep reasoning, evidence, and limitations with your artifact.
lessons.sourceName: Google Machine Learning Crash Course — further reading

questions.explanation: A useful prompt specifies the task and intended audience. A request to explain a topic to a beginner is more directed than a request to explain everything.

questions.prompt: For the activity “Write a prompt explaining fractions to a beginner using two examples.”, which approach demonstrates learning?
options: Treat an unverified generated response as final evidence.

lessons.title: Output format
lessons.subtitle: Week 6: Prompting with purpose
lessons.body:
A requested format helps make output usable: a table, checklist, short paragraph, or questions. Format instructions do not guarantee accuracy.

lessons.title: Examples and revisions
lessons.subtitle: Week 6: Prompting with purpose
lessons.body:
An example can demonstrate the desired response style. A focused revision asks for a specific change rather than repeating an unclear request.

Offline practice: Draft an example response and a revision request that reduces jargon without removing the main idea. Write your reasoning before looking at the quiz answers. Record one limitation or uncertainty. You can use paper or local notes; an online AI tool is optional.

Recap: explain yesterday’s key idea from memory, then check your notes. After a break, start with this recap and the first small step of today’s activity.

Complete all three quiz questions before moving on.
takeaways: An example can demonstrate the desired response style. A focused revision asks for a specific change rather than repeating an unclear request.
Apply the idea through the offline activity.
Keep reasoning, evidence, and limitations with your artifact.

lessons.title: Prompt portfolio
lessons.subtitle: Week 6: Prompting with purpose
lessons.body:
A prompt portfolio records the task, prompt, expected result, checks, and revision. It helps you explain why an approach worked.

Offline practice: Save three prompts with offline sample responses and a note on what you would verify online. Write your reasoning before looking at the quiz answers. Record one limitation or uncertainty. You can use paper or local notes; an online AI tool is optional.

Recap: explain yesterday’s key idea from memory, then check your notes. After a break, start with this recap and the first small step of today’s activity.

Complete all three quiz questions before moving on.

Weekly completion task: save this week’s practice artifact. Confirm four steps: explain a key idea (recap); complete the practice activity (practice); record what you would verify and where (plan); show your artifact and explain one improvement (demonstrate).
takeaways: A prompt portfolio records the task, prompt, expected result, checks, and revision. It helps you explain why an approach worked.
Apply the idea through the offline activity.
Keep reasoning, evidence, and limitations with your artifact.
